answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to one real registered beehive marked by a uniquely engraved onyx stone and kept beneath a named willow grove. A licensed apiarist inspects one hive per day in person, logging its health and honey yield, while random dawn spot-checks summon the holder to open that exact hive on camera within hours. One operator cannot tend two hives at once, and the apiary fee in outside money doubles per further hive on the same funding trail, so each extra fake identity costs another colony, another dawn inspection, another human, and twice the prior fee.
